99218948f6.fzText: Students should 1) obtain non-zero grade from each of the project presentations and labs AND 2) Collect at least 20/49 from midterm + lab work + attendance AND 3) attend at least 29 lectures. Attendance is taken with a signature in every lecture hour. Signing the attendance sheet in the name of another student is a disciplinary offence under Law 2547. weekly: Digital information. Number systems and conversions. Binary, octal and hexadecimal.
Logic gates, truth tables and Boolean algebra. Timing diagrams and propagation delay. Canonical forms, cost and levels of a two-level circuit, the look-up table.
CMOS gates: the transistor as a switch, inverter, NAND, NOR, RC origin of delay, power. Delay in gate networks: critical path and hazards. Minimization with Karnaugh maps.
Inside the FPGA: look-up tables, slices, carry chain, routing, clock network, bitstream. Introduction to VHDL: entity, architecture, concurrent statements, processes, simulation.
Combinational building blocks: decoders, encoders, multiplexers, tristate buffers, comparators, parity.
Binary arithmetic: signed numbers, two's complement, overflow and codes. Adders and subtractors, ripple-carry delay, carry-lookahead.
Tutorial and problem session (Republic Day holiday).
Feedback: the ring oscillator and the latch. Flip-flops, setup time, hold time, clock-to-output delay. Midterm review.
The clock: generation, PLL, clock tree, clock enables, jitter, clock constraints. Registers, shift registers and counters. Maximum clock frequency and the Vivado timing report.
Synchronous design discipline: clock skew, metastability, synchronizers, debouncing, reset. Finite state machine design methodology.
Finite state machine design examples and their timing.
Finite state machines in VHDL, state encoding. Clock domain crossing: synchronizers, handshake, Gray codes, asynchronous FIFO.
Digital system design: datapath and control.
Timing closure: pipelining, throughput and latency. Review of the course.

Spectral analysis of IQ data: DFT, PSD, spectrogram, windows. FIR/IIR, mixing, decimation. Amplitude and angle modulation (skim). Lab 1: recover a signal from an offline IQ capture.
RTL-SDR bring-up (streaming vs file, gain, clipping). Leakage, windows, and frequency estimation below the bin grid. Lab 2: estimate a tone frequency in noise.
Detection vs estimation. Cramer-Rao bound. Matched filter. Pulsed interference: energy detection, blanking.
Correlation and direct-sequence spreading. Lab 3: recover a live signal under pulsed interference.
Phase/frequency lock (PLL/FLL). Arrays and spatial combining.
Lab 4: known spreading sequence under a jammer. Optional: beamforming over multiple collaborating receivers.
Adaptive filtering. Tracking a moving interferer. Lab 5: recover a wide signal under a drifting tone.
Resolution limits. Interpolation vs subspace methods. Two tones inside one DFT bin.
Independent component analysis. Lab 6: remove a closely spaced interferer, then separate mixed audio sources.
Design-project case study (search then lock). Project mid-check.

weekly: Introduction to Wireless Communications: Wireless services and requirements; technical challenges (fading, ISI, spectrum); system design overview; noise-limited systems and the link budget.

Signal Model and Theoretical Foundations: Complex baseband representation; discrete-time signal model; SNR, capacity and other performance metrics; DFT and frequency-domain view. Self-study recap: complex algebra, probability, estimation and detection basics.

Propagation Mechanisms and Statistical Channel Description: Free-space attenuation, reflection, diffraction, scattering; path loss and shadowing; small-scale fading: Rayleigh, Rice, Nakagami; Doppler spectra; fading margins.

Wideband and Directional Channels; Channel Models: Delay dispersion, coherence bandwidth and time, WSSUS assumption, condensed parameters (delay spread, angular spread); deterministic vs. stochastic models; standardized (3GPP-type) channel models.
Modulation and Demodulation: Signal-space picture; PAM/QAM/PSK families; optimum receivers; error probability in AWGN and in flat-fading channels; error floors in dispersive channels (qualitative).

Diversity and a Channel-Coding Overview: Diversity sources (space, time, frequency, polarization); selection, switched and combining diversity; MRC and its connection to SIMO beamforming; fundamentals of coding and information theory; modern code families (LDPC, polar) at overview level.
OFDM: Multicarrier principle; cyclic prefix and DFT-based implementation; time–frequency resource grid; practical issues: PAPR, windowing, synchronization and impairments. MIDTERM EXAM (Weeks 1–6).
Capacity of Point-to-Point MIMO Channels: Impact of power and bandwidth on capacity; SIMO and MISO capacities; MIMO capacity with CSIT (waterfilling) and without; multiplexing vs. array gain.

Line-of-Sight MIMO and Antenna Arrays: Array response vectors, ULA geometry; beamforming and beam patterns; grating lobes; near-field vs. far-field; rank of LOS MIMO channels. Practical antenna considerations.

Non-Line-of-Sight MIMO: Fading Capacity and Channel Estimation Rayleigh fading MIMO channels; outage vs. ergodic capacity; slow vs. fast fading regimes; block fading; pilot-based (LS/MMSE) channel estimation.

Multi-User MIMO and Massive MIMO: Uplink and downlink system models; capacity results and duality (overview); linear receive combining and transmit precoding (MRT/ZF/MMSE); massive MIMO: channel hardening, favorable propagation, pilot contamination.

Multiple Access and Cellular Networks: FDMA/TDMA/OFDMA; random access (ALOHA, CSMA); duplexing (TDD/FDD); frequency reuse and cell planning; inter-cell interference; scheduling and power control basics.

MIMO-OFDM and Practical Implementations: Capacity of wideband MIMO-OFDM channels; clustered propagation and hybrid analog–digital beamforming; practical terminology (codebooks, CSI acquisition in TDD/FDD, antenna ports); RF hardware overview: PAs, phase noise, ADC resolution.

Real Systems and Outlook: How the course maps to 5G NR (frame structure, beam management, massive MIMO in NR) and Wi-Fi (OFDM/MIMO evolution to 802.11ax); beyond-5G directions: reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, integrated sensing and communication.
